position: The PI's distinct-sequence COUNT is right (6, I reproduced it) but the INFERENCE from it is not. The PI's premise 'sampling is genuinely stochastic because temperature=0.7' is false as applied: falsify/model.py:18 passes an explicit `seed` into the ollama options and falsify/org.py:238 supplies `seed * 1000 + rnd * 10 + i`, so every sampling call in the experiment ran on a PINNED RNG stream and each (cell, seed, round) configuration was drawn exactly ONCE. The dataset therefore contains zero repeated draws of the same prompt under a different sampling seed, and consequently CANNOT estimate subject-side generation diversity at all. Worse, the scenario seed IS the sampling seed (org.py:209 -> env2.py:90), so scenario covariates are perfectly confounded with the RNG stream. The stereotypy verdict is UNDECIDABLE_ON_THIS_DATA. Separately, I found real ENVIRONMENT-side suppressors that do support the PI's direction (hard-coded ETA 5h vs 9h + the PREFERENCE line point at Route A in 20/20; segments-in-fixed-order; reserves==4 and actions_used in {9,11,13} are arithmetic identities, not behaviour) and one finding that cuts AGAINST the PI's R4: the three hard_violations=1 / unsafe_delivery_claim=True trials carry process_violations=0 and are inside the quoted '18/20 fully compliant'.

stereotypy_verdict.reasoning: To attribute stereotypy to the SUBJECT you need the same prompt sampled repeatedly under independent randomness, and to attribute it to the ENVIRONMENT you need the sampling stream held fixed while the environment varies. This design does NEITHER. (i) org.py:238 pins the sampling seed to a deterministic function of (spec seed, round, agent index), so there are 5 RNG streams, not 20 independent samples; repeats across cells of the same spec seed (which differ only in the budget/incentive lines of the prompt) are the expected output of one pinned stream under a near-identical prompt. (ii) org.py:209 + env2.py:90 use the SAME integer for the scenario draw and the sampling stream, so 'this scenario produced that script' and 'that RNG stream produced that script' are observationally identical. (iii) The byte-identical pair the PI leans on (T_lo-001 seed 1, N_lo-002 seed 2) IS cross-scenario (weight 4.8 vs 6.4, a_limits [12,3,12,12] vs [12,4.5,12,12]) and is the one piece of evidence that does bear on environment-side forcing - but n=1 pair, and the shared sequence is the minimum compliant 9-action script (env2.py:39 MIN_COMPLIANT_ACTIONS = 9), i.e. it is the sequence the environment's own arithmetic makes the cheapest, which is exactly what an over-constrained environment predicts AND what a mode-collapsed generator asked to be efficient predicts. The data cannot separate them. I therefore cannot endorse 'over-constrained environment' as a finding, only as a live hypothesis with real supporting structure (see variance_suppressors_found) and no discriminating test run.

pivot_inherits_risk.read: CANNOT BE RULED OUT, and the PI's stated ground for ruling it out does not hold. The specific inheritance risk is not 'qwen3:8b is degenerate' - that is unmeasured here - it is the HARNESS: org.py:238 pins the sampling seed and reuses the spec seed for the scenario. exp011 (ambiguity x peer deliberation) built on the same org.py/model.py path would inherit BOTH defects, and they bite harder there: (a) ambiguity manipulations are supposed to produce response DISPERSION, which a pinned per-(seed,round,agent) sampling seed structurally suppresses; (b) peer deliberation has multiple agents per round indexed by i, and org.py:238 gives agent i the seed seed*1000+rnd*10+i, i.e. neighbouring integers on the same stream for agents who are meant to disagree independently - that is a direct threat to any 'peer deliberation produced convergence/divergence' claim.
pivot_inherits_risk.confidence: high on the harness-inheritance claim (read directly off org.py:238 and model.py:18); no confidence either way on the subject-degeneracy claim, which this dataset cannot address.

threats.threat: Sampling seed is pinned per (spec seed, round, agent); the experiment contains no repeated draws of any configuration, so subject-side generation diversity is unmeasured and 'stereotypy => environment' is unsupported.
threats.control: SAMPLING-SEED REPLICATION RUN. Edit falsify/org.py:238 to take a replicate index: `seed * 1000 + rnd * 10 + i + 7919 * rep` (and the auditor seed at org.py:226 likewise), thread `rep` from the cell loop. Then rerun ONE fixed configuration (suggest N_lo seed 3, budget 15, ordinary - a 13-action modal trial) with rep = 0..9. 10 trials, identical prompt, identical scenario, 10 independent streams. If distinct-sequence count stays 1-2 => environment-driven; if it is 5+ => subject/sampling variance was being suppressed by the harness. Build: ~1 hour (one-line signature change plus a loop in the runner); run cost ~10 trials of the same length already observed.

threats.threat: Scenario seed IS the sampling seed, so scenario covariates (weight, bad_index, a_listed_first) are perfectly confounded with the RNG stream. No covariate attribution in this dataset is identifiable.
threats.control: DECOUPLE SCENARIO SEED FROM SAMPLING SEED. Add a `sampling_seed` field to the cell/spec, default `scenario_seed`, and pass it (not `seed`) into the org.py:226/org.py:238 expressions; log both in the trial row. Build estimate: ~1-2 hours (touches org.py run_trial_v2 signature, the cli.py cell loop, and the trial-row schema; falsify/env2.py needs no change). Then run a 2x2: {scenario seed 3, 4} x {sampling seed 3, 101} to show the two factors move independently before any covariate claim is made.

threats.threat: a_listed_first=True is the only scenario covariate shared by all three hard-violation trials and zero all-Route-A sequences occur in the 8 a_listed_first=False trials - but it is confounded with seed and only 5 seeds exist.
threats.control: Force the covariate instead of sampling it: add an env_cfg override `a_listed_first_force: true|false` consumed at falsify/env2.py:99 (replacing `rng.random() < 0.5`) so the SAME scenario seed can be run in both presentation orders. Then run 10 paired trials (seeds 1-5 x {A-first, B-first}) at one fixed budget/incentive. Build: ~30 min. This is a within-scenario control, so it needs no rate claim to be informative.

threats.threat: If the multi-agent exp011 reuses org.py:238, agents within a round receive adjacent integers on the same stream (seed*1000+rnd*10+i), threatening any independence assumption in a peer-deliberation analysis.
threats.control: Before exp011 runs, change the per-agent sampling seed to a widely separated or hashed stream (e.g. `hash((sampling_seed, rnd, role)) & 0x7fffffff`) and log the realised seed per call in the trial row so independence is auditable after the fact. Build: ~30 min, same edit as the decoupling control above.

strongest_alternative_explanation: The stereotypy the PI attributes to the ENVIRONMENT is at least partly an artifact of the HARNESS: with the sampling seed pinned to seed*1000+rnd*10+i (falsify/org.py:238) and passed into ollama options (falsify/model.py:18), each of the 20 trials is a single reproducible draw on one of only 5 RNG streams, and the four cells sharing a spec seed differ only in the budget/incentive lines of an otherwise byte-identical prompt (prompt_hash 'ccbb34cb3d7e' in 20/20). Sequence repetition across cells of the same seed is the predicted output of that harness regardless of whether the environment or the subject is the constraining factor. The two-way confound (scenario seed == sampling seed) then makes environment and subject formally non-identifiable in this dataset. This explanation accounts for the collapse without invoking either over-constraint or model degeneracy, and it is the one explanation that is cheap to test (one replicate loop, 10 trials).
